extracted.intended_audience: United States Military Governor in Germany (Gen. Lucius D. Clay) and U.S. occupation authorities
extracted.subtask_description: A U.S. State/War/Navy Departments directive to the Military Governor in occupied Germany specifying objectives, authorities, and detailed policy requirements across political, legal, economic, social, and cultural domains for occupation administration and reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of This Directive
rubrics_metrics.description: This directive ... constitutes a statement of the objectives of your Government in Germany and of the basic policies to which your Government wishes you to give effect from the present time forward. It supersedes JCS 1067/6 and its amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issued to the commanding general of U.S. occupation forces and Military Governor; frames the objectives and basic policies to be implemented in Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of Military Government
rubrics_metrics.description: Your authority as Military Governor will be broadly construed and empowers you to take action consistent with relevant international agreements, general foreign policies of this Government and with this directive, appropriate or desirable to attain your Government’s objectives in Germany or to meet military exigencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pending arrangements for treatment of Germany as an economic and political unit, exert every effort to achieve economic unity with other zones; authority includes actions necessary for objectives and military exigencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States Policy Toward Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: The basic interest of the United States throughout the world is just and lasting peace. Such a peace can be achieved only if conditions of public order and prosperity are created in Europe as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Europe requires economic contributions of a stable and productive Germany while restraining revival of destructive militarism; U.S. proposes treaty for continuing disarmament and demilitarization and commits to maintain a U.S. occupation army as long as foreign occupation continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demilitarization
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue disarmament and demilitarization provisions; emphasize economic measures needed to rehabilitate Germany and maintain measures to complete and effectively maintain the disarmament and demilitarization of Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No relaxation in the program; action required to create conditions making revival of militarism impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States Political Objectives in Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an objective ... that there should arise in Germany as rapidly as possible a form of political organization and a manner of political life which, resting on a substantial basis of economic well-being, will lead to tranquillity within Germany and will contribute to the spirit of peace among nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help lay economic and educational bases of a sound German democracy; encourage democratic efforts and prohibit activities which would jeopardize genuinely democratic developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: German Self-Government
rubrics_metrics.description: You will continue to promote the development in Germany of institutions of popular self-government and the assumption of direct responsibility by German governmental agencies, assuring them legislative, judicial and executive powers consistent with military security and the purposes of the occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor establishment of federal German states (Laender) with a central government of limited powers; avoid imposing external historical forms of democracy; ultimate constitutional form left to German people under democratic processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-Zonal German Administrative Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending the establishment of central German administrative agencies and of a central German government, you will continue, consistent with objectives of Paragraph 6, to make arrangements with other zonal commanders for the creation and operation of inter-zonal German administrative agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with other zone commanders to create inter-zonal bodies to implement common policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political Parties: Authorization and Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: You will adhere to the policy of authorizing and encouraging all political parties whose programs, activities and structure demonstrate their allegiance to democratic principles. Authorized parties shall be competitive, voluntary associations with accountable leaders and no privileged status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every authorized party should have the right freely to state views and present candidates; tolerate no curtailment of that right unless the party adopts undemocratic practices, in which case restrict or withdraw rights; urge Control Council recognition of nationwide parties and uniform treatment in all zones; advocate quadripartite supervision of political activities and elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denazification and Non-Discriminatory Treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities should afford non-discriminatory treatment to duly authorized political parties and pursue decisions on denazification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement denazification decisions in your zone; ensure equal treatment and prevent revival of National Socialist influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: War Crimes Program
rubrics_metrics.description: You will make every effort to facilitate and bring to early completion the war crimes program subject to the conclusions and recommendations ... contained in the judgment of the International Military Tribunal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support prosecution and processing of war crimes as directed by international judgments and Control Council conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts and Judicial Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise such supervision over German courts as is necessary to prevent the revival of National Socialist doctrines, to prohibit discrimination on grounds of race, nationality, creed or political belief, to enforce Control Council Proclamation No. 3 and compliance with Military Government legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster judicial independence by allowing freedom in interpretation and application of law, limit Military Government control to minimum consistent with accomplishment of objectives; protect civil rights of detained persons, require specific charges and fair trials, limit detention to security necessities, permit communication and periodic review of detention, and permit extension of German jurisdiction over non-Military-Government-interest cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislation: Power of Disapproval
rubrics_metrics.description: You will exercise your power of disapproval over German legislation only when such legislation conflicts with the legislation or policies of Military Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use disapproval sparingly and only for conflict with Military Government policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Movement of Persons and Displaced Persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement decisions (23 April 1947) regarding migration to other countries of displaced persons unwilling to be repatriated; retain overall responsibility for their care, maintenance and protection pending movement; utilize the IRO to maximum extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define 'displaced persons' per IRO Constitution; hold German authorities responsible for nationals of former enemy countries; assist German authorities in resettlement programs; permit inter-zone exchange and free movement for temporary purposes consistent with security; prioritize returnees who can contribute to peaceful reconstruction; permit only categories of Germans to leave as agreed by Allied agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prisoners of War: Return
rubrics_metrics.description: Press in the Control Council for the earliest possible return of all German prisoners of war still located in territories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement Council of Foreign Ministers decision of 23 April 1947 regarding repatriation of POWs.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Economic Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic objectives: (a) eliminate industry used solely to manufacture and reduce industry used chiefly to support arms production; (b) exact reparations for losses suffered as a consequence of German aggression; (c) encourage Germans to rebuild a self-supporting state devoted to peaceful purposes, integrated into Europe's economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide general policy guidance, assist development of balanced foreign trade, insure German efforts contribute to U.S. Government objectives while leaving rehabilitation primarily to German people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic Disarmament and Reparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Desire fulfillment of Potsdam principles regarding reparation and industrial disarmament; level of industry agreed for reparation removals should not permanently limit Germany's industrial capacity; Germans should not be denied right to develop resources consistent with disarmament; no reparation greater than Potsdam Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid financing reparations by increasing U.S. outlay or postponing self-sustaining German economy; reaffirm proceeds of authorized exports used first for payment of authorized imports; seek Control Council recognition of compensation for property taken or destroyed under disarmament agreements; attempt to avoid removing foreign-owned plants where German-owned plants available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Restore identifiable property (other than gold and transport essential to minimum German economy) to governments of countries from which taken, consistent with Control Council agreements on restitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not consent to extensive replacement programs of looted property if replacement would consume reparations, harm German economy, or cultural heritage; turn over monetary gold to Tripartite Gold Commission; make available looted personal property for rehabilitation of non-repatriable victims; compensate victims of National Socialist persecution in German currency and designate successor organizations for heirless property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic Unity and Recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure agreement to treat Germany as an economic unit, formulate common policies affecting Germany as a whole, establish central administrative agencies to implement policies for finance, transport, communications, agriculture, economics, trade, etc.; adopt production and foreign trade program directed toward increasing standard of living and attaining self-sustaining German economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize coal, food and export goods; allocate indigenous output and approved imports to carry out production program; insure full payment for exports (other than reparations/restitution) in approved imports or usable foreign exchange and pool export proceeds first for German import needs, second to compensate occupying powers per agreed terms and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Policies and Controls
rubrics_metrics.description: View finances on a sound basis and attainment of financial stability in Germany as essential to recovery; endeavor to have Control Council adopt uniform financial policies in conformity with directive objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pending agreement, policies include: control international financial transactions to keep Nazi influence out and prevent capital flight; supervise public expenditures and taxation to ensure consistency with objectives; prevent establishment of centralized banking or undue concentration of financial power while encouraging central authority for currency production and technical supervision; use German economic resources to reduce U.S. appropriated fund expenditures; maintain accounts reflecting financial operations; calculate occupation costs distinguishing internal vs external costs for eventual settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agriculture, Forestry and Fishing Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Insure carrying out and completion of land reform in your zone in 1947; require German authorities to adopt policies and practices maximizing production and providing for effective collection and distribution of agricultural products; adopt similar policies for forestry and fishing resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on maximizing production and efficient distribution as part of overall recovery and food supply objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic Institutions: Industry, Cartels, Cooperatives, Trade Unions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending agreement among occupying powers prohibit cartels and cartel-like organizations; effect dissolution of combines, holding companies and interlocking directorates that dominate industry; permit cooperatives if voluntary and democratic; refrain from interfering with public ownership choices except to ensure free democratic decision; limit new foreign investment; insure property and production subject to Control Council and Military Government law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit formation of trade unions and work councils if democratic and responsible to membership; encourage unions to support adult education; allow collective bargaining within wage/price control limits; permit machinery for voluntary settlement of industrial disputes; coordinate with other zone commanders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural Objectives and Re-education
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-education of the German people is integral to developing democratic government and restoring a stable peaceful economy; no forcible break in cultural unity but foster regional traditions and international cultural relations to overcome spiritual isolation imposed by National Socialism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate cultural objectives among occupying powers, encourage German initiative and responsible participation, expedite international cultural relations and travel of persons useful for cultural reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage and assist development of educational methods, institutions, programs and materials designed to further the creation of democratic attitudes and practices; require Laender authorities to adopt educational programs to develop a healthy, democratic educational system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate National Socialist, militaristic and aggressively nationalistic influences, practices and teachings in schools; use education to foster democratic attitudes and prevent recurrence of totalitarian indoctrination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious Affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Give freedom to Germans to decide questions concerning the constitution, organization and amalgamation of ecclesiastical bodies; permit and assist formation of purely ecclesiastical organizations; take necessary action to permit religious activity and travel in accordance with occupation policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect religious freedom and permit ecclesiastical organization while ensuring actions consistent with broader occupation objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monuments, Fine Arts and Archives
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect and permit German authorities to protect and preserve property of cultural institutions dedicated to religion, charity, education and the perpetuation of National Socialist victims' memory; apply appropriate measures to safeguard monuments, fine arts and archives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect collections and endowments; permit access and preservation except for institutions specifically devoted to perpetuation of National Socialism; apply appropriate archival and museum protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange through other ... the development by the Germans of public information and press policies consistent with occupation objectives (fragmentary in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervise public information to prevent resurgence of hostile ideologies and to aid re-education and democratic development; coordinate with other occupying powers on press and information policies.
